findings: The candidate preserves the recovered source contract: reverse the linked-list nodes from m through n with a single forward traversal, without pretending that indexing or invalid-input behavior was preserved in the note.
The 1-based inclusive range, non-null input, valid-range precondition and in-place mutation are explicitly labelled as candidate API assumptions rather than source facts.

The head-insertion loop maintains a sufficient invariant: before stays immediately ahead of the reversed region, current stays at that region's tail, and current.next is the next node to move to the front.

The implementation does not rescan from the list head and uses only a dummy node plus a constant number of references, so the stated linear-time and O(1)-auxiliary-space bounds match the implementation.

Seven fixed boundary cases plus 5000 deterministic randomized valid ranges are checked against an array-subrange-reversal oracle that is structurally different from the linked-list algorithm and additionally rejects extra nodes or cycles.
The candidate correctly keeps n beyond list length outside its declared contract instead of inventing a source-backed behavior; a production API could add explicit validation separately.
The follow-ups are specific to the pointer invariant, one-pass interpretation, dummy-node boundary and space argument.
No online-judge attribution, production history, hidden size bound or other unstated source constraint is fabricated. Human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
